title: Psalms Bible Quiz - Chapter 105
description: Ten questions on Psalms 105: the call to remember his works, the covenant with Abraham, Joseph sold as a slave, the plagues in Egypt and the care in the desert.

questions.text: What does the psalmist tell the people to make known among the peoples?
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:1 says: give thanks to Yahweh, call on his name, and make his doings known among the peoples.

questions.text: Besides his strength, what are the people told to seek forever more?
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:4 says: seek Yahweh and his strength, seek his face forever more.

questions.text: Who are called "his chosen ones" in the opening verses?
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:6 addresses the offspring of Abraham, his servant, and the children of Jacob, his chosen ones.

questions.text: Which land did God promise as "the lot of your inheritance"?
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:11 quotes God: "To you I will give the land of Canaan, the lot of your inheritance."

questions.text: What did God say when he reproved kings for the sake of his people?
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:14-15 says he reproved kings for their sakes: "Don't touch my anointed ones! Do my prophets no harm!"

questions.text: According to the psalm, what was Joseph sold as?
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:17 says God sent a man before them: Joseph was sold for a slave.
Psalms 105:18 says they bruised his feet with shackles, and his neck was locked in irons.

questions.text: What did the king make Joseph after setting him free?
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:21 says the king made him lord of his house and ruler of all his possessions.

questions.text: How far did the swarming frogs reach?
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:30 says their land swarmed with frogs, even in the rooms of their kings.

answers.text: Even into the rooms of their kings
Even into the temples of their gods

questions.text: What did God spread for a covering over his people?
questions.explanation: Psalms 105:39 says he spread a cloud for a covering, and fire to give light in the night.
